clinician.trajectory_summary: A 58-year-old patient presented with burning micturition, fecaluria, pneumaturia, abdominal pain, episodes of cystitis, and dysuria. On admission, the patient was vitally stable. Laboratory tests showed mild leukocytosis and raised urea and creatinine, indicating infection and renal impairment. Contrast-enhanced pelvic CT was contraindicated due to raised creatinine; therefore, ultrasound and barium enema were performed. Ultrasound revealed a 1.5 cm defect between the sigmoid colon and urinary bladder with passage of echogenic material, confirming a fistulous tract. Although the barium enema report was not documented, the ultrasound findings combined with clinical signs strongly support the diagnosis of entero-vesical fistula likely secondary to diverticulosis.
